messages:
tara_support: FYI customer 'AcmeSearch' reports embeddings shape changed after we respun a pinned variant — used to be 2048, now 1024. golang client errors out with shape mismatch. Sentry: SENT-4421. Request id from customer: req_0x9f3. Any quick triage tips?

mike_infra: Which pinned tag/version did they have? Was the respin just infra or did it include a model artifact change?

tara_support: They were pinned to rwd-open-embed-v2@2026-03-01-respin (artifact hash a1b2c3). Notes say "respin: int8 pack optimization". Customer shows index failures during batch upsert.

sam_ml: Quantization/packing shouldn't change vector dimensionality. More likely either the model artifact produced a different head (wrong checkpoint) or the model metadata artifact.meta.vec_size is wrong. Can you dump the model_config.json for that exact artifact?

mike_infra: I checked runtime logs around the time the customer got the failure. Found: 
```
[2026-03-18T11:02:33Z] embed_pipeline: processed req=req_0x9f3 model=rwd-open-embed-v2@2026-03-01-respin vec_len=1024 batch_id=17
[2026-03-18T11:02:33Z] batcher: flush triggered pad_mode=truncate batch_size=64 avg_seq=128
```
No obvious kernel errors, just vec_len reported as 1024.

deploy-bot: Deployed pinned variant rwd-open-embed-v2@2026-03-01-respin to customer-facing pool at 2026-03-18T10:59:00Z (deploy id dpl-77b).

tara_support: Customer sent sample curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-embed-v2","input":["search query 1","search query 2"]}'
```

sam_ml: I can repro locally by pulling that exact artifact. Quick repro steps I used:
1) checkout artifact a1b2c3 -> model_config.json shows "vec_size": 1024
2) run local inference with small text -> returns 1024 float32 vector
So the artifact was produced with 1024 dim.

mike_infra: That suggests the respin accidentally swapped in an older training checkpoint or we built a smaller head variant. Was there an automated variant dedup step in the release pipeline?

tara_support: The customer expects backcompat to 2048. They have indexed many embeddings; ingest fails and search quality dropped. They've asked for ETA.

sam_ml: Short-term mitigations: (A) Roll the customer back to their prior pinned artifact (rwd-open-embed-v2@2026-02-20) if available; (B) runtime compatibility shim that upcasts/pads vectors to 2048 by appending zeros — only for ingestion paths and marked in logs (not ideal but buys time).

mike_infra: I'll check pin history and whether rollback is allowed for that tenant. If rollback can't be done fast, we can enable a per-tenant compatibility layer for up to N requests/min. I'll prepare runbook steps and risk notes.

sam_ml: I'll diff the model bundles (a1b2c3 vs previous good hash f9e8d7). If it's just a metadata mismatch we can hotpatch the metadata server to advertise vec_size correctly; if binary weights are actually 1024 we need to restore prior artifact.

tara_support: Triage plan posted to the customer: 1) We are investigating root cause and will provide ETA within 3 hours. 2) Asking them to pause ingest for new data to avoid index churn. 3) Requesting a sample upsert payload and the index schema.

mike_infra: Action items: @sam_ml - grab both artifacts and run vector dim diff. @mike_infra - check deployment pins and rollback permission. I'll open ENG ticket ENG-1958 and assign.

sam_ml: :thumbsup: I found that build pipeline had a transient tag collision; CI accidentally promoted an older training run that used a distilled head (1024). Looks like the respin included that. I'll prepare backfill notes.

tara_support: Notified customer of plan: immediate rollback candidate + optional compatibility pad if rollback delayed. They acknowledged. Will follow up with updates here.

mike_infra: Rolling plan: if rollback succeeds, we'll coordinate with customer to replay missed upserts. If rollback blocked, enable pad-shim and issue hotfix to model registry to prevent duplicate promotion.

tara_support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated and paste rollback runbook once ready.
